notes: Phase 1 scope only: Storage, KeyVault, AppServices (Function/Web App TLS+HTTPS), Defender plan enablement. Everything else stays at Propose until Phase 2 (Intelligence Layer) exists to route it responsibly.

environmentResolution._comment: Fail-closed: if a subscription/RG isn't tagged, treat it as the highest-risk bucket, never assume NonProd/Low.

killSwitch._comment: When enabled=true (or the -KillSwitchPath file exists), every category is forced to Propose regardless of the matrix below. This is the emergency stop.

Storage.description: Storage account TLS, secure transfer (HTTPS-only), public blob access

KeyVault.description: Key Vault soft delete, purge protection, RBAC authorization
KeyVault._rollbackNote: Soft delete and purge protection are irreversible once enabled (Azure platform behavior, not a toolkit limitation). RBAC-auth switch is reversible but re-breaks any access policies still in use.

AppServices.description: Function App / Web App HTTPS-only and minimum TLS version

Defender._scopingWarning: Fix-EnableDefenderPlans.ps1 iterates ALL subscriptions the identity can see internally (Set-AzContext per subscription) regardless of what scope you invoke it with. Until it accepts a -SubscriptionId parameter, the orchestrator hard-overrides this category to Propose/Escalate only -- see Invoke-Phase1AutoRemediation.ps1 comments. Do not change this in the matrix without fixing the script first.
